steps: Megalithic burials in Andhra cluster in the south: Rayalaseema (Chittoor, Anantapuramu, Tirupati) and Krishna.
Options (a), (c) and (d) all name these southern districts; only (b) names a north-coastal district, Visakhapatnam.
Cist burials are a southern feature, not a Visakhapatnam one, so (b) is the incorrect statement.
-> answer (b)
fact: Andhra megaliths (cists, dolmens, sarcophagi) are concentrated in Rayalaseema and Krishna, not in Visakhapatnam.

steps: (A) is certain: Hala's Gatha Saptasati is a Prakrit anthology of love poems, so it is true. Strike (b) and (d).
(B): Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in Paisachi Prakrit. The legend says he refused to write in Sanskrit. So (B) is false.
-> answer (c) (A) true, (B) false
fact: Gunadhya's Brihatkatha was written in Paisachi, not Sanskrit; Hala's Gatha Saptasati is Prakrit love poetry.

steps: (c) is a known fact: the Ikshvakus married into the Saka (Western Kshatrapa) house of Ujjain.
(d) is also known: Nagarjunakonda reached its Buddhist peak under Virapurushadatta. (a) is true too: the Puranas call them Sriparvatiyas.
(b) claims descent from Ayodhya. Their own inscriptions make no such claim; modern scholars suggested the link because of the name.
-> answer (b)

underline.why: the record says no such thing

fact: The Vijayapuri Ikshvakus' inscriptions do not claim descent from the Ayodhya Ikshvakus; the Puranas call them Sriparvatiyas.

steps: Link the title to its book: 'Janasraya' appears in 'Janasrayi Chhandovichiti', a prosody work of the Vishnukundin period.
That work is attached to Madhavavarma, the greatest Vishnukundin king, who bore the title Janasraya.
-> answer (d) Madhavavarma
fact: Madhavavarma of the Vishnukundins bore the title Janasraya (cf. Janasrayi Chhandovichiti).

steps: The Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada is recorded in the Musinikonda grant of the first Eastern Chalukya age.
Its builder, Ayyana Mahadevi, was the queen of the dynasty's founder, Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
Strike Jatachoda Bhima, who was a later usurper, and Gunaga Vijayaditya, who ruled in the 9th century.
-> answer (c) Kubja Vishnuvardhana
fact: Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana, built the Nedumba Vasati (Jain) at Vijayawada.

steps: Madhavavarma, the strongest Vishnukundin king, is credited with moving the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru near Eluru.
Strike Manchana Bhattaraka, a minor figure, and Govindavarma, an early ruler.
APPSC's final key accepts both (a) Vikramendravarma and (b) Madhavavarma.
-> answer (b) Madhavavarma
fact: Madhavavarma moved the Vishnukundin capital to Denduluru (final key also accepts Vikramendravarma).

steps: Test (A): Roman trade peaked in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE, which is the Satavahana period, and fell away after it. (A) is false. Strike (a), (b) and (c).
Test (R): ship-motif coins are a Satavahana signature (Yajnasri Satakarni), and later rulers did not issue them. (R) is true. The extreme word 'No' leans false, but here the fact overrides it.
-> answer (d) (A) false, (R) true
fact: Indo-Roman trade flourished under the Satavahanas and declined after them; ship-motif coins are Satavahana.

steps: Anchor on a: the Billa Surgam caves are in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, not Anantapuramu. So a is incorrect.
Strike every option without a: (b) 'b and c' and (d) 'c only' go.
Decide b: Belum Caves (Nandyal) are the second-longest cave system in India, so b is correct and (a) 'a and b' goes.
-> answer (c) a only
fact: Billa Surgam caves are in Kurnool (Nandyal) district; Belum caves are India's second-longest.

steps: Place the dates: the Satavahanas ruled from about the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE. The Kakatiyas rose in the 12th century CE.
Dynasties about 800 years apart cannot have a marriage alliance, so (d) is impossible.
(a) Andhrabhrityas, (b) bilingual Prakrit and Tamil-Brahmi coins and (c) patronage of both religions are standard facts.
-> answer (d)
fact: Satavahanas (c. 1st c. BCE-3rd c. CE) and Kakatiyas (12th-14th c.) never overlapped.

steps: I is certain: Nannaya began the Andhra Mahabharatam. Strike (c) 'II and III', the only option without I.
II: tradition credits Nannaya with Andhra Sabda Chintamani, a Sanskrit grammar of Telugu, so keep II. Strike (b) 'I and III'.
III: Rajaraja Narendra's Nandampudi grant went to Narayana Bhatta, Nannaya's associate, not to Nannaya. III is false, so strike (d).
-> answer (a) I and II

underline.text: Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya

fact: The Nandampudi grant of Rajaraja Narendra was given to Narayana Bhatta, not Nannaya.

steps: Use the generation chain: Vimaladitya married Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja I. Their son Rajaraja Narendra married Ammangadevi, the daughter of Rajendra I. Their son Rajendra Chalukya married Madhurantaki, the daughter of Rajendra II.
II and III fit the chain, so they are correct. Strike (b), (c) and (d), which all mark II or III as incorrect.
I names Saktivarma, Vimaladitya's elder brother, in place of Vimaladitya.
-> answer (a) Only I
fact: Kundavai (daughter of Rajaraja Chola I) married Vimaladitya, not Saktivarma.

steps: Anchor on c: Chalukya Bhima built the Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama, and the god's name echoes the king's. So c is correct.
Strike every option that marks c incorrect: (a) 'a and c', (b) 'b and c' and (d) 'c only'.
Check: the Biccavole Rajarajeswara temple belongs to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's period, not Rajaraja Narendra's.
-> answer (c) b only

underline.text: Chalukya Bhima constructed Bhimeswara Swamy temple at Draksharama
Raja Raja Narendra constructed Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole

fact: Draksharama Bhimeswara was built by Chalukya Bhima I; the Biccavole temples belong to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's time.

steps: The Chalukya-Chola style belongs to the Vengi region (coastal Andhra).
Brihadeeshwara (Thanjavur) is pure imperial Chola, and Padmakshi (Hanamkonda) is a Kakatiya-region temple. Strike both, and with them (d) 'All of the above'.
Draksharama Bhimeswara in Vengi mixes Pallava and early Chalukya features.
-> answer (b) Draksharama temple
fact: Draksharama temple exemplifies the Chalukya-Chola style of Vengi.

steps: The surest pair: Tikkana wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam before his Mahabharata, so c-II.
Only code (b) has c-II. Strike (a), (c) and (d).
Check: Ketana wrote Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first Telugu grammar in Telugu, and Marana wrote Markandeya Puranam.
-> answer (b) a-III, b-I, c-II, d-IV
fact: Tikkana wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam; Ketana wrote Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam; Marana wrote Markandeya Puranam.

steps: Sarvalokasraya and Vishnuvardhana are Eastern Chalukya (Vengi) titles. A Chola viceroy who took them ruled Vengi in the Chalukya style.
Strike Parantaka Chola, a 10th-century ruler from before the Chalukya-Chola union.
Recall the viceroy crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama): Mummadi Chola.
-> answer (c) Mummadi Chola
fact: Chola viceroy Mummadi Chola took the titles Sarvalokasraya Sri Vishnuvardhana and was crowned at Draksharama.

steps: Test (A): at Tikkana's request, Ganapatideva put Manumasiddhi II back on the Nellore throne. (A) is true. Strike (d).
Test (R): a king who had to be restored by a Kakatiya overlord was not at the height of power. The Nellore Chodas peaked under Tikka I. (R) is false.
-> answer (c) (A) true, (R) false

underline.text: reinstated on the throne by Ganapatideva

fact: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II at Tikkana's request; the Nellore Chodas peaked under Tikka I.

steps: Anchor on II: Kakatiya temples clearly follow the later Chalukya style. Strike (b) 'I and III only'.
III is also a standard fact: the Thousand Pillar temple is a trikuta shrine to Rudreswara, Vasudeva and Surya. Strike (a) 'I and II only'.
I: the early Kakatiyas were Jain patrons before turning Saiva, so I is true as well. The 'only' options fall.
-> answer (d) I, II, III
fact: The Thousand Pillar temple is a trikuta shrine (Rudreswara, Vasudeva, Surya) in the later Chalukya style.

steps: Gangadevi, Kampana's queen, is known for one work: Madhura Vijayam, on the conquest of Madurai.
Marichi Parinayam was written by Mohanangi, Krishnadevaraya's daughter, so the pair in (a) is wrong.
The other pairs are standard: Molla's Ramayanam, Timmakka's Subhadra Kalyanam and Tirumalamba's Varadambika Parinayam.
-> answer (a)
fact: Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam; Marichi Parinayam is by Mohanangi.

steps: Latest: Pedakomati Vema Reddi (1402-20) is the last great Kondavidu Reddi. Strike (a), which starts with D, and (c), which ends with A.
Earliest: Anavota came right after the founder Prolaya Vema, and Kumaragiri ruled after Anavema. Strike (b), which starts with Kumaragiri.
-> answer (d) C, B, A, D
fact: Kondavidu Reddi order: Prolaya Vema, Anavota, Anavema, Kumaragiri, Pedakomati Vema.

steps: The surest pair: Dignaga, the Buddhist logician, wrote Pramana Samuccaya, so d-IV. Codes (a) and (c) keep it; strike (b) and (d).
Then Pavuluri Mallana translated the mathematics text Ganitasara Sangraham, so a-II. Strike (a), which has a-I.
-> answer (c) a-II, b-I, c-III, d-IV
fact: Pavuluri Mallana translated Ganitasara Sangraham; Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kreedabhiramam; Dignaga wrote Pramana Samuccaya.

steps: The surest pair: the Motupalli abhaya-sasana for sea traders was issued by Ganapatideva, so d-II. Codes (a) and (c) keep it.
Both codes give c-I (Bayyaram tank, Mailamba), so decide on b: the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription is Rudradeva's, so b-IV. Strike (a), which has b-III.
-> answer (c) a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II
fact: Motupalli = Ganapatideva; Anumakonda = Rudradeva; Bayyaram = Mailamba; Sanigaram = Prola.

steps: Statement b says the nayankara system was 'introduced by' Prataparudra. Claims that a ruler introduced a system lean false: the system was older, and Prataparudra only expanded it.
Mark b incorrect. Strike (b) 'a and c' and (c) 'a only', which leave b out.
Decide c: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of Srisailam, which is accepted. Strike (a).
-> answer (d) b only
fact: The Kakatiya nayankara system predates Prataparudra; he expanded it.

steps: Srinatha wrote Telugu kavyas: Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam and Palnati Veera Charitra.
'Bhanam' (bhana) is a one-act Sanskrit play form. Madana Vilasa Bhanam is by Vamana Bhatta Bana.
-> answer (b) Madanavilasabanam

underline.why: bhana: Sanskrit play, Vamana Bhatta Bana

fact: Madana Vilasa Bhanam is by Vamana Bhatta Bana, not Srinatha.

steps: The conquest of coastal Andhra means the Kalinga campaign against the Gajapatis, which pushed north to Simhachalam.
Krishnadevaraya set up his jayastambha at Potnuru near Simhachalam.
Udayagiri and Kondaveedu were forts captured on the way, and Nagarjunakonda has no link.
-> answer (b) Potnuru
fact: Krishnadevaraya's victory pillar after the Kalinga campaign stands at Potnuru near Simhachalam.

steps: (B) is certain: the tribute zamindars paid to the Company was peshkash. Strike (b) and (c).
(A): moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and looms, not a salt tax. (A) is false.
-> answer (d) (A) false, (B) true
fact: Moturpha was a tax on professions and trades; peshkash was the zamindars' tribute.

steps: Test (A): coastal Andhra stayed largely quiet in 1857. The key accepts (A) as true.
Test (R): Nizam Afzal-ud-Dowla did side with the British, so (R) is true.
Does R explain A? The Nizam ruled Hyderabad, while coastal Andhra was under the Madras Presidency. His attitude cannot explain Andhra's calm, so R is not the explanation.
-> answer (b)
fact: In 1857 coastal Andhra was in the Madras Presidency, so the Nizam's pro-British stand does not explain its calm.

steps: 'Founded by <person>' claims are worth checking. The Crescent (1844) was founded by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty.
Mutnuri Krishna Rao is famous as the editor of Krishna Patrika. His name has been moved onto another paper, so (b) is incorrect.
The final key also accepts (c), the disputed 'first Telugu political newsweekly' claim.
-> answer (b)
fact: The Crescent (1844) was founded by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty; Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika.

steps: Bipin Chandra Pal's April 1907 tour sparked the Kakinada riots, so the tour comes first: b-III (April 1907) and a-II (July 1907).
Only code (c) has b-III. Strike the rest.
Check: the Kotappakonda riots were in February 1909 and the Tenali bomb case in April 1909.
-> answer (c) a-II, b-III, c-I, d-IV

underline.text: Bipin Chandra Pal's tour in Andhra

fact: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907; the Kakinada riots followed in July 1907.

steps: Place each range: Papikondalu are on the Godavari gorge, Nallamala in Kurnool and Prakasam, and Palakondalu in Kadapa. Strike all three.
The Srikakulam-Odisha border hills are the Mahendragiri range.
-> answer (d) Mahendra Girulu
fact: The Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam are called the Mahendragiri hills.

steps: Latest: the States Reorganisation Commission (1953) comes last. Strike (d), which starts with D.
Earliest: the Dhar Commission (1948). Only (b) starts with B.
Check: Visalandhra Mahasabha in 1949 and Swami Sitaram's fast in 1951 fit the middle.
-> answer (b) B, A, C, D
fact: Order: Dhar Commission 1948, Visalandhra Mahasabha 1949, Sitaram's fast 1951, SRC 1953.

steps: Test (A): the Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Hippon. Hawkins belongs to Surat and Jahangir's court (1608). (A) is false. Strike (a), (b) and (c).
Test (R): the Golconda Sultan did allow the English factory at Machilipatnam, so (R) is true.
-> answer (d) (A) false, (R) true
fact: The Globe came to Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Hippon; Hawkins went to Jahangir's court.

steps: Remember the titles: Viswanatha is 'Kavi Samrat', Sri Sri is the revolutionary 'Mahakavi', and Boyi Bhimanna wrote Dalit drama.
Rayaprolu started a new era of Telugu poetry with Bhava Kavitvam, as Nannaya started the first, so he is 'Abhinava Nannaya'.
-> answer (b) Rayaprolu Subbarao
fact: Rayaprolu Subbarao, father of Bhava Kavitvam, is called Abhinava Nannaya.

steps: Sri Sri claimed the century ('ee satabdam naadi'), so he is the poet of the century, not the millennium. Strike (b).
Gurram Jashuva, 'Navayuga Kavi Chakravarthi', was honoured as Sahasrabdi Kavi, the poet of the millennium.
-> answer (c) Gurram Jashuva
fact: Gurram Jashuva was hailed as the Poet of the Millennium (Sahasrabdi Kavi).

steps: Gabbilam is Jashuva's most famous work, and examiners often swap the famous title in for the one that actually won the award.
His 1964 Sahitya Akademi award was for 'Kreestu Charitra', so (b) is incorrect.
-> answer (b)

underline.why: famous work swapped in: Kreestu Charitra

fact: Jashuva won the 1964 Sahitya Akademi award for Kreestu Charitra, not Gabbilam.

steps: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam are seaside villages on the Prakasam coast, known for salt pans.
They were centres of the 1930 salt satyagraha. Textiles, indigo and sugar have no such coastal link.
-> answer (d) Salt
fact: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam on the Prakasam coast are salt-producing centres.

steps: The surest pair: the 1st Andhra Mahasabha (Bapatla, 1913) was presided over by Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma, so a-III.
Only code (a) has a-III. Strike (b), (c) and (d).
-> answer (a) a-III, b-II, c-IV, d-I
fact: The first Andhra Mahasabha (Bapatla, 1913) was presided over by Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma.

steps: Latest: zamindari abolition (1948 Act) comes last. Strike (c), which ends with A, and (d), which starts with D.
Earliest: the Company acquired Guntur in 1788, before the Battle of Padmanabham (1794) and Munro's Ryotwari (about 1820). Strike (a).
-> answer (b) B, C, A, D

underline.text: Abolition of Zamindari settlement in Andhra

fact: Order: Guntur acquired 1788, Padmanabham 1794, Ryotwari about 1820, zamindari abolished 1948.

steps: The Maidavolu (Mayidavolu) plates of Sivaskandavarman are the classic early Pallava Prakrit grant from Andhra.
The Manchikallu record of Simhavarman belongs to the same early Pallava group.
-> answer (a) Pallavas
fact: Maidavolu and Manchikallu inscriptions are early Pallava Prakrit records.

steps: The surest pair: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam is the oldest Telugu library, founded in Hyderabad in 1901, so b-III. Codes (a) and (c) keep it.
Both give a-II (Vignana Chandrika, 1906). Decide c: the key pairs the Andhra Council of Research with Hyderabad, 1922 (c-IV). Strike (c).
-> answer (a) a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I
fact: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in Hyderabad in 1901.

steps: Anchor on III: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in Hyderabad in 1901, not Kovvur in 1916. III is false.
Strike every option that contains III: (b), (c) and (d) 'All of the above'.
-> answer (a) I, II, IV only
fact: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam: Hyderabad, 1901; Andhra Patrika: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, 1908.

steps: a is certain: the Communists (Sundarayya) championed Visalandhra.
Visalandhra is itself an integrated linguistic state, so c, which says they opposed such states, contradicts a. c is incorrect.
Strike (b) and (c), which mark a. Statement b is true because of the Telangana armed struggle, so strike (a) too.
-> answer (d) c only

underline.text: opposed the formation of integrated linguistic States

fact: The Communists were the main champions of Visalandhra, an integrated linguistic state.

steps: A committee set up by the Madras State Government in 1949 would naturally be chaired by its Chief Minister.
The Madras Chief Minister in 1949 was P. S. Kumaraswamy Raja. Prakasam was a member, and the others were not in charge then.
-> answer (b) Kumaraswamy Raja
fact: The 1949 Partition Committee of Madras was chaired by CM P. S. Kumaraswamy Raja.

steps: Earliest: Damodaram Sanjivaiah (1960-62), the first Dalit CM. Latest: Tanguturi Anjaiah (1980-82).
Only (b) starts with B and ends with A. Strike the rest.
Check: Brahmananda Reddy (1964-71) came before P. V. Narasimha Rao (1971-73).
-> answer (b) B, D, C, A
fact: CM order: Sanjivaiah 1960, Brahmananda Reddy 1964, P. V. Narasimha Rao 1971, Anjaiah 1980.

steps: The two middle values are 40:60 and 60:40.
Andhra was the larger region, so it got the larger share. Strike 40:60 and the even 50:50; 70:30 would be too lopsided for a pact meant to reassure Telangana.
-> answer (c) 60 : 40
fact: The 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement fixed Cabinet seats at 60% Andhra : 40% Telangana.

steps: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu is Viswanatha Satyanarayana's epic, and it won the 1970 Jnanpith, the first for Telugu.
C. Narayana Reddy won later (1988, Viswambhara). Strike (a); the other two never won it.
-> answer (c) Vishwanatha Satyanarayana
fact: Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the first Telugu Jnanpith (1970) for Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu.

steps: Recall the charter: Elizabeth I granted it on 31 December 1600. The middle-value rule does not apply to this famous date.
-> answer (a) 1600
fact: The English East India Company was chartered on 31 December 1600.

steps: Tirupati is in Rayalaseema, so look for a party with a Rayalaseema base during the 1953 capital debate.
That party was the Krishikar Lok Party. The Praja Socialist and Kisan Mazdoor parties had no such regional stand.
-> answer (c) Krishikar Lok Party
fact: In 1953 the Krishikar Lok Party demanded Tirupati as Andhra's capital.

steps: The surest pair: Pattabhi Sitaramayya's home base was Machilipatnam (Andhra Bank, Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala), so d-IV. Codes (a) and (c) keep it.
Next: Bulusu Sambamurti was the Kakinada leader, so a-I. Strike (c).
-> answer (a) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
fact: 1930 salt satyagraha: Sambamurti at Kakinada, Dandu Narayana Raju at Mattapalem, Kasi Viswanadham at Vadarevu, Pattabhi at Machilipatnam.

steps: Yanam is still part of the Union Territory of Puducherry, which is made up of the former French possessions.
Rajahmundry, Hamsaladivi and Ongole have no French link.
-> answer (c) Yanam
fact: Yanam was a French settlement until 1954 and is now part of Puducherry.

steps: Do not pick 'Andhra' just because the dynasty is Andhra. The earliest Satavahana records are the Naneghat (Naganika) and Nasik inscriptions.
Both are in the western Deccan near their capital Pratishthana (Paithan).
-> answer (a) Maharashtra
fact: The early Satavahana inscriptions (Naneghat, Nasik) are in Maharashtra.

steps: The Justice Party governed Madras Presidency in 1920-37, so the university must date from those years.
Andhra University (1926) fits. SV University (1954), Padmavati (1983) and Telugu University (1985) are all later.
-> answer (b) Andhra University
fact: Andhra University was founded in 1926 under the Justice Party ministry.

steps: 'Desamante matti kadoi' is Gurajada Apparao's patriotic song.
It belongs to his poetry collection Mutyala Saralu, named after the metre he made popular.
-> answer (d) Mutyala Saralu
fact: Gurajada's 'Desamante matti kadoyi' is from Mutyala Saralu.

steps: The surest pair: the Ashtanga Margam (eightfold path) is Buddhism, so b-ii. Codes (c) and (d) keep it.
Next: the linga is Saivism, so c-iv. Strike (d), which has c-i.
-> answer (c) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
fact: Triratna = Jainism, Ashtanga Marga = Buddhism, Linga = Saivism, nature worship = animism.

steps: The surest pair: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organised the Rama Dandu volunteers, so a-iii.
Only code (b) has a-iii. Strike (a), (c) and (d).
Check: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy was called 'Kaviraju', so d-iv.
-> answer (b) a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv
fact: Duggirala = Rama Dandu; Parvataneni Veeraiah = Pedanandipadu; Kaleswara Rao = Naa Jeevitha Katha; Tripuraneni = Kaviraju.

steps: The surest pair: Veyipadagalu is Viswanatha Satyanarayana's novel, so d-iv.
Only code (d) has d-iv. Strike (a), (b) and (c).
Check: Kanyasulkam is by Gurajada (c-i) and Mahaprasthanam by Sri Sri (b-ii).
-> answer (d) a-v, b-ii, c-i, d-iv
fact: Veyipadagalu = Viswanatha; Kanyasulkam = Gurajada; Mahaprasthanam = Sri Sri; Japaneeyamu = Sriram Veerabrahmam.

steps: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription is in the Jain cave complex of Udayagiri-Khandagiri, and it opens with a salutation to the Arhats.
-> answer (a) Jainism
fact: Kharavela of Kalinga patronised Jainism (Hathigumpha, Udayagiri caves).

steps: The Undavalli caves are near Vijayawada, the core of the Vishnukundin kingdom, and date to the 4th-5th centuries.
Strike the Kakatiyas and Reddis (much later) and the Rashtrakutas (not based in Andhra).
-> answer (a) Vishnukundins
fact: The Undavalli rock-cut caves are attributed to the Vishnukundins.

steps: The 'Blue Water Policy' means ruling the sea rather than land. It was the policy of Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy.
-> answer (a) Portuguese
fact: Almeida's Blue Water Policy was Portuguese.

steps: Match each person to what he is known for: Cotton built the dams, Brown worked on Telugu literature, and Noble founded the Machilipatnam college. Only Munro was a revenue administrator.
Munro became Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema) in 1800.
-> answer (a) Sir Thomas Munro
fact: Thomas Munro was the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema).

steps: C. P. Brown is the great Telugu scholar of the 1800s, and his Telugu-English dictionary came out in 1852.
H. H. Wilson worked on Sanskrit, and Munro and Wellesley were administrators.
-> answer (a) C.P. Brown
fact: C. P. Brown compiled the first Telugu-English dictionary (1852).

steps: APPSC's final key gives Krishna Patrika (1902, Machilipatnam). Satyadoota (1835) is often called the first Telugu periodical, but the key did not accept it.
-> answer (d) Krishna Patrika
fact: APPSC treats Krishna Patrika (1902) as the first Telugu newspaper; Satyadoota (1835) is an earlier periodical.

steps: This is the same fact as the 'Globe' question: the English set up their first east-coast factory at Machilipatnam in 1611.
-> answer (b) Machilipatnam
fact: The English set up their first factory on the east coast at Machilipatnam in 1611.

steps: Do not mix this up with Bobbili (1757), where the French and Vizianagaram fought Bobbili. Strike (b).
At Padmanabham (1794) the Company killed Vijayarama Raju II of Vizianagaram.
-> answer (c) English and Vizianagaram Zamindars
fact: The Battle of Padmanabham (1794) was between the English and Vizianagaram's Vijayarama Raju II.
